paper.title_en: Communication Complexity of Distributed Unitary Synthesis
paper.abstract_en: We study space-bounded communication complexity for unitary implementation in distributed quantum processors, where we restrict the number of qubits per processor to ensure practical relevance and technical non-triviality. We model distributed quantum processors using distributed quantum circuits with nonlocal two-qubit gates, defining the distributed communication complexity of a unitary as the minimum number of such nonlocal gates required for its realization, up to permutations of data qubit positions. Our contributions are twofold. First, for general <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-qubit unitaries, we improve upon the trivial <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$O(4^{n})$ </tex-math></inline-formula> communication bound. With <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$k$ </tex-math></inline-formula> pairwise-connected processors (each having <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$n/k$ </tex-math></inline-formula> data qubits and <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m$ </tex-math></inline-formula> ancillas), we prove the communication complexity satisfies <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$O\left ({ \max \{4^{(1-1/k)n - m}, n\}}\right)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> —e.g., <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$O(2^{n})$ </tex-math></inline-formula> when <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$m=0$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$k=2$ </tex-math></inline-formula>—and show this upper bound is tight. We also extend the analysis to approximation and general topology models. Second, for special unitaries, we demonstrate that both Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) and Clifford circuits admit linear upper bounds on communication complexity within the exact model. This outperforms the trivial quadratic communication complexity that applies to these two unitaries. In the approximation model, QFT’s communication complexity reduces drastically from linear to logarithmic, while Clifford circuits still require at least linear communication. These results provide fundamental insights into optimizing communication for distributed quantum unitary implementation, advancing the feasibility of large-scale DQC systems.
